questions.question: On roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles when used on roadways. Bicyclists and motorists must follow the same rules of the road.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow line to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the vehicle ahead is driving under the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing. You cannot cross them to pass other vehicles. You can only cross double yellow lines when turning into or out of a driveway or business entrance.

questions.question: How can you avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while turning on a curve may cause you to skid.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Try to fight it.
Take a break.
Take some caffeine pills.

questions.explanation: Pull over at the first rest stop or service area to nap, stretch, or change drivers. Caffeine pills and energy drinks are not safe replacements for rest and can make driving more dangerous.

questions.question: If a vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes loses traction on a slippery road, what should the driver do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.
Lightly tap the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: With Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), press down hard on the brake pedal and hold it while steering to safety. The ABS automatically pumps the brakes faster than you can. Reducing brake pressure or pumping the brakes will turn off the ABS.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for drunk drivers.
Curves ahead.
Slippery when wet.
Apply your brakes quickly.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: Is it sometimes unsafe to drive at 10 mph?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Drive slower than the speed limit when conditions require it. Bad traffic, weather, or visibility may require you to drive as slowly as 10 mph or slower.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Slow down.
Drive more quickly.
Drive the speed limit, with caution.
Not drive more quickly than 20 mph.

questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or sleet begins. These conditions make roads slippery. Drive slower than the speed limit when road conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Highway signs that warn about hazardous conditions are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead. Obey warning signs for your safety. Ignoring them may cause an accident.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Watch for drunk drivers.
Dangerous curve ahead.
Bump in the road ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns drivers to be careful when the pavement is wet because roads become slippery and harder to control.

questions.question: Is it safe to pull in front of a large truck that is slowing or stopping?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Never pull in front of a large truck that is slowing or stopping. The driver has planned their braking distance based on the space in front of them. If you suddenly cut in front, you take away that space and could cause a crash.

questions.question: When dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should slow down and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly. Other drivers also need to see you better in these conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The crossing is controlled. Keep your regular speed.
Look and listen. Be ready to stop if needed.
Stop at the tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look and listen. Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing, you must look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before you cross.

questions.question: What does a yellow left turn arrow mean?

options.text: Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending soon.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: A yellow left turn arrow means two things: the protected turn is about to end, and you must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: After passing a car, you have enough space to return to the driving lane when:

options.text: The other driver signals for you to move back.
You look over your shoulder and see the car behind you.
You can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure there is a safe distance between your car and the car you passed. When you see both of its headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.explanation: The only way to sober up is to give your body time to remove the alcohol from your system. Eating, drinking coffee, or other methods do not speed up this process.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines down the center of a road mean that passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: Which of the following increases crash risk for distracted drivers?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.explanation: Using a cell phone, radio, or CD player can distract you from driving and increase your risk of a crash.

questions.question: You should use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days to:

options.text: Keep your engine warm.
Help other drivers see your vehicle.
Warn others about the bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help other drivers see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, other drivers have trouble seeing your vehicle. Headlights make you more visible. If you need windshield wipers, you must also use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the side with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the side with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the side with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass only from the side next to the broken line.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road ahead curves left then right.
The road ahead curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right then left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers the road will curve right first, then curve left. Slow down and be ready to turn.

questions.question: If a driver sees an animal on the roadway:

options.text: No special action is required.
The driver should honk their horn.
The driver should pass the animal as closely as possible.
The driver should be very cautious.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver should be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid scaring it.

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk at the bicyclist to let them know you're trying to pass.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you get a chance to pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Rush ahead to pull in front of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down when passing a bicyclist and give them plenty of space. Bicyclists have less protection than car drivers. Passing too quickly can make them lose control.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Sit in your car and wait for help.
Use your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Sound your horn at passing motorists.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers right away. Exit the road safely and park where other drivers can see you. Lift your hood to show your car is broken down.

questions.question: You may avoid the risks of alcohol-related crashes by:

options.text: Deciding before you start drinking that you are not going to drive.
Simply saying, "No thanks, I'm driving," if someone offers you a drink.
Calling a taxi.
Doing any of the above.

questions.explanation: Plan ahead before you drink. Decide not to drive, say no to drinks, or call a taxi. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it hard to make safe choices later.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge.
Winding road ahead.
Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes are about to become one lane.

questions.question: You come to an intersection that is blocked by other traffic. You should:

options.text: Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
Sound your horn to make the cars move up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if you cannot drive all the way through. Wait until the road ahead is clear so you don't block the intersection.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle:

options.text: Beep your horn.
Expect the child to be in total control of the bicycle.
Expect the unexpected.

questions.explanation: Children on bicycles are unpredictable and may change direction suddenly. They and their bicycles are small and easy to miss. Watch for anything unexpected.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. You should:

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before you enter a curve. Braking while turning can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and blind spots before passing. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane when you can see the other car's front bumper in your mirror.
